question: With a uniform speed, a car covers a distance in 16 hours. Had the speed been increased by 20 km/h, the same distance would have been covered in 12 hours. The total distance covered by the car is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When distance is constant, speed and time are inversely proportional.

Ratio of Time = 16 : 12 = 4 : 3 ⇒ Ratio of Speed = 3 : 4

Difference in speed ratio (1 unit) = 20 km/h

Original speed = 3 units = 60 km/h

Total distance = 60 km/h × 16 h = 960 km

**∴ The correct answer is 960 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken at original speed = 16 hours

Time taken at increased speed = 12 hours

Increase in speed = 20 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time
